text:
maya: quick sync — I'm updating the performance dashboard to show a compact view that includes: TTFT (first token latency), tokens/sec, and p95 tail. before I crank on panels I want to confirm the canonical metric names we should use and who can run a short profiler on staging. PR I'm going to reference: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/234

sam: +1. for metric names I propose we standardize on: `first_token_latency_ms` (histogram), `tokens_emitted_total` (counter), and `requests_total` (counter). keep labels: model, model_variant, env, shard.

lily: agree with naming. for p95 queries I'd use PromQL like this in grafana:
```
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(first_token_latency_ms_bucket[5m])) by (le, model, model_variant))
```
and tokens/sec per instance:
```
sum(rate(tokens_emitted_total[1m])) by (model) / sum(rate(requests_total[1m])) by (model)
```
Note: divide after the sum to avoid per-instance skew.

maya: that PromQL looks good. a couple of follow-ups: (1) do we want p95 over 5m or 1h on the main panel? (2) is `first_token_latency_ms` currently exported from runtime or do we need a small change?

sam: runtime already emits `first_token_latency_ms` but it's in microseconds on the exporter right now (legacy). we should convert to ms in the exporter to avoid confusion. i'll open a tiny runtime PR to change units.

ops-jen: for the dashboard: default view = p95 over 5m for recent troubleshooting, and a second smaller panel with 1h p95 for trend. set unit to "ms" and use 90s refresh. also add an alert rule: p95_first_token_latency_ms{env="production",model=~"open-.*"} > 200 for 5m -> page.

lily: small profiling ask: the p95 seems to spike when cache miss ratio > 10%. can someone run a quick bench to reproduce with cache off vs on? bench-bot can you schedule? :eyes: 

bench-bot: scheduling run: `bench/ttft --model=open-red-13b --seq=1024 --runs=40 --cache=off` and `--cache=on`. queued on staging. I'll post results here when complete.

maya: thanks. also for the dashboard panel json, prefer explicit label `model_variant` in legend like `{{model}}/{{model_variant}}` so product teams can differentiate quantized vs full fp16.

sam: noted. i'll make exporter unit change + add label normalization (strip `:q4_0` suffix into model_variant). will link PRs.

bench-bot: finished: results -> https://bench.rw/results/ttft/1762005432. summary: p95 cache-off = 320ms, cache-on = 140ms, tokens/sec ~ 220 tok/s steady for this model. attached CSV.

ops-jen: that's a big delta — we should annotate the dashboard with a note about KV cache being a major contributor. Also add a small text panel with guidance: "if p95 > 250ms, check cache miss ratio and routing fallbacks".

maya: perfect. i'll open the dashboard PR with the panels, the alert, and the annotation. Assigning review to sam and ops-jen. i'll include the bench link and the PromQL snippets.

sam: i'll review today. thanks for coordinating. :thumbsup:

lily: if you want I can add a small recording of `perf` flame graphs from the staging run into the PR as well. could help root cause if we see kernel stalls.

maya: please do — that would be super helpful. I'll assign you on the PR.

ops-jen: last note — add an ownership field in the dashboard annotation: owner=eng-runtime. helps page routing.

maya: done, thanks everyone. follow-ups: sam runtime PR, maya dashboard PR, lily flame graph upload. ping here when done. :party:
